---- MODULE W4Od10m1p2t2 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANTS N, TOTAL
ASSUME N \in Nat /\ N >= 2 /\ TOTAL \in Nat

VARIABLES inner, outer, depot, siding
vars == <<inner, outer, depot, siding>>

Blocks == 1..N

RECURSIVE SumF(_, _)
SumF(f, S) == IF S = {} THEN 0
              ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE
                   IN f[x] + SumF(f, S \ {x})

TokensOnLoop(f) == SumF(f, Blocks)

Init == /\ inner = [b \in Blocks |-> 0]
        /\ outer = [b \in Blocks |-> 0]
        /\ depot = TOTAL
        /\ siding = 0

Advance(f) == \E i \in Blocks :
                /\ f[i] > 0
                /\ LET j == (i % N) + 1 IN
                     f' = [f EXCEPT ![i] = @ - 1, ![j] = @ + 1]

AdvanceInner == /\ Advance(inner) /\ UNCHANGED <<outer, depot, siding>>
AdvanceOuter == /\ Advance(outer) /\ UNCHANGED <<inner, depot, siding>>

DispatchInner == /\ depot > 0
                 /\ inner' = [inner EXCEPT ![1] = @ + 1]
                 /\ depot' = depot - 1
                 /\ UNCHANGED <<outer, siding>>
DispatchOuter == /\ depot > 0
                 /\ outer' = [outer EXCEPT ![1] = @ + 1]
                 /\ depot' = depot - 1
                 /\ UNCHANGED <<inner, siding>>

ReturnInner == /\ inner[N] > 0
               /\ inner' = [inner EXCEPT ![N] = @ - 1]
               /\ depot' = depot + 1
               /\ UNCHANGED <<outer, siding>>
ReturnOuter == /\ outer[N] > 0
               /\ outer' = [outer EXCEPT ![N] = @ - 1]
               /\ depot' = depot + 1
               /\ UNCHANGED <<inner, siding>>

ToSiding == /\ depot > 0
            /\ depot' = depot - 1 /\ siding' = siding + 1
            /\ UNCHANGED <<inner, outer>>
FromSiding == /\ siding > 0
              /\ siding' = siding - 1 /\ depot' = depot + 1
              /\ UNCHANGED <<inner, outer>>

Next == \/ AdvanceInner \/ AdvanceOuter
        \/ DispatchInner \/ DispatchOuter
        \/ ReturnInner \/ ReturnOuter
        \/ ToSiding \/ FromSiding

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TokenPoolConserved ==
    TokensOnLoop(inner) + TokensOnLoop(outer) + depot + siding = TOTAL
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS N = 2 TOTAL = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT TokenPoolConserved
nl:
A metropolitan subway is divided into signalling blocks arranged as two independent circular lines, an inner loop and an outer loop, each with a fixed number of blocks. A train may occupy a block only if it holds the movement token for that block. Movement tokens are physical objects: they are never manufactured on the fly and never discarded. Both loops draw their tokens from a single shared depot pool, so the two lines compete for the same finite supply. At each step a token can advance one block forward along its loop, a fresh token can be dispatched from the depot into the entry block of either loop, or a token that reaches a loop's exit block can be handed back to the depot, or a spare token can be shunted between the depot and a maintenance siding. Because the loops share the depot, an operator must be sure the tokens are merely being shuffled between loops, entry blocks, exit points, the depot, and the maintenance siding, and are never created or lost.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the total number of movement tokens summed over both loops, the shared depot, and the maintenance siding always equals the fixed number the system started with.

ASSUME CAP \in Nat /\ MAXEPOCH \in Nat

vars == <<north, south, reserve, epoch>>

TypeOK == /\ north \in 0..CAP
          /\ south \in 0..CAP
          /\ reserve \in 0..CAP
          /\ epoch \in 0..MAXEPOCH

Init == /\ north = 0
        /\ south = 0
        /\ reserve = CAP
        /\ epoch = 0

ShedNorth == /\ north > 0
             /\ north' = north - 1 /\ reserve' = reserve + 1
             /\ UNCHANGED <<south, epoch>>
ShedSouth == /\ south > 0
             /\ south' = south - 1 /\ reserve' = reserve + 1
             /\ UNCHANGED <<north, epoch>>
RestoreNorth == /\ reserve > 0
                /\ north' = north + 1 /\ reserve' = reserve - 1
                /\ UNCHANGED <<south, epoch>>
RestoreSouth == /\ reserve > 0
                /\ south' = south + 1 /\ reserve' = reserve - 1
                /\ UNCHANGED <<north, epoch>>

ReconfigN2S == /\ epoch < MAXEPOCH
               /\ north > 0
               /\ north' = north - 1 /\ south' = south + 1
               /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
               /\ UNCHANGED reserve
ReconfigS2N == /\ epoch < MAXEPOCH
               /\ south > 0
               /\ south' = south - 1 /\ north' = north + 1
               /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
               /\ UNCHANGED reserve

Next == \/ ShedNorth \/ ShedSouth
        \/ RestoreNorth \/ RestoreSouth
        \/ ReconfigN2S \/ ReconfigS2N

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TotalMegawattsConserved == north + south + reserve = CAP

cfg_text:
CONSTANTS CAP = 3 MAXEPOCH = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT TotalMegawattsConserved
INVARIANT TypeOK
nl:
A regional power authority runs a load shedder across two electrically independent grids, a northern grid and a southern grid, that both draw generation from one shared spinning reserve. Power is measured in fixed megawatt units that are conserved: shedding a unit of demand does not destroy power, it simply returns that generation capacity to the shared reserve, and restoring demand pulls capacity back out of the reserve. The controller operates in numbered configuration epochs; each time the topology is rebalanced the epoch counter advances by one and exactly one megawatt unit of committed generation is migrated from one grid to the other, again conserving the total. At each step the controller may shed a unit from either grid back to the reserve, restore a unit from the reserve to either grid, or perform an epoch reconfiguration that shifts a committed unit between the two grids. Because both grids feed from the same reserve, the authority must confirm that megawatts are only ever moved among the northern grid, the southern grid, and the reserve.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the committed generation of the northern grid plus that of the southern grid plus the shared reserve always equals the fixed total generation capacity, in every epoch.

---- MODULE W4Od15m2p0t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Firms
ASSUME Firms # {}

VARIABLES pstate, coord, granted, msgs
vars == <<pstate, coord, granted, msgs>>

Init == /\ pstate = [f \in Firms |-> "idle"]
        /\ coord = "free"
        /\ granted = "none"
        /\ msgs = {}

Request(f) == /\ pstate[f] = "idle"
              /\ msgs' = msgs \cup {[type |-> "req", firm |-> f]}
              /\ UNCHANGED <<pstate, coord, granted>>

Prepare(f) == /\ coord = "free"
              /\ [type |-> "req", firm |-> f] \in msgs
              /\ coord' = "granting"
              /\ granted' = f
              /\ msgs' = (msgs \ {[type |-> "req", firm |-> f]})
                            \cup {[type |-> "prep", firm |-> f]}
              /\ UNCHANGED pstate

Vote(f) == /\ pstate[f] = "idle"
           /\ [type |-> "prep", firm |-> f] \in msgs
           /\ pstate' = [pstate EXCEPT ![f] = "prepared"]
           /\ msgs' = (msgs \ {[type |-> "prep", firm |-> f]})
                          \cup {[type |-> "vote", firm |-> f]}
           /\ UNCHANGED <<coord, granted>>

Commit(f) == /\ coord = "granting"
             /\ granted = f
             /\ pstate[f] = "prepared"
             /\ [type |-> "vote", firm |-> f] \in msgs
             /\ pstate' = [pstate EXCEPT ![f] = "holding"]
             /\ msgs' = msgs \ {[type |-> "vote", firm |-> f]}
             /\ UNCHANGED <<coord, granted>>

Release(f) == /\ pstate[f] = "holding"
              /\ granted = f
              /\ pstate' = [pstate EXCEPT ![f] = "idle"]
              /\ coord' = "free"
              /\ granted' = "none"
              /\ UNCHANGED msgs

Next == \E f \in Firms :
          Request(f) \/ Prepare(f) \/ Vote(f) \/ Commit(f) \/ Release(f)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ExclusiveOrderBook ==
    \A f \in Firms : pstate[f] = "holding" => granted = f
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS Firms = {f1, f2}
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT ExclusiveOrderBook
nl:
A stock exchange runs an opening auction in which several member firms contend for exclusive write access to the single central order book while it is being sealed and matched. Only one firm at a time may hold this critical write lock. Access is granted through a two-phase commit driven by a coordinator: a firm first requests the lock, the coordinator prepares a candidate firm by sending it a prepare message, the firm votes to accept, and only when the coordinator receives that vote does it commit the grant so the firm begins holding the lock; when the firm is done it releases and the coordinator becomes free again. The exchange network does not guarantee ordering, so prepare messages, votes, and requests sit in an unordered pool and may be delivered in any order. Because a mis-sequenced or duplicated message must never cause two firms to hold the book at once, the exchange tracks which firm the coordinator has committed to and treats that as the sole legitimate holder.
SAFETY PROPERTY: at any instant at most one member firm holds the exclusive order-book write lock, namely the one firm the coordinator has committed the grant to.

---- MODULE W4Od7m8p2t5 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANTS Bays, TOTAL
ASSUME Bays # {} /\ TOTAL \in Nat

VARIABLES ship, bay, bayLock, phase, target
vars == <<ship, bay, bayLock, phase, target>>

RECURSIVE SumB(_)
SumB(S) == IF S = {} THEN 0
           ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN bay[x] + SumB(S \ {x})

Init == /\ ship = TOTAL
        /\ bay = [b \in Bays |-> 0]
        /\ bayLock = [b \in Bays |-> "free"]
        /\ phase = "idle"
        /\ target = "none"

AcquireCoarse == /\ phase = "idle"
                 /\ \E b \in Bays :
                      /\ bayLock[b] = "free"
                      /\ bayLock' = [bayLock EXCEPT ![b] = "coarse"]
                      /\ target' = b
                 /\ phase' = "coarse"
                 /\ UNCHANGED <<ship, bay>>

AcquireFine == /\ phase = "coarse"
               /\ target \in Bays
               /\ bayLock' = [bayLock EXCEPT ![target] = "fine"]
               /\ phase' = "fine"
               /\ UNCHANGED <<ship, bay, target>>

Unload == /\ phase = "fine"
          /\ target \in Bays
          /\ ship > 0
          /\ ship' = ship - 1
          /\ bay' = [bay EXCEPT ![target] = @ + 1]
          /\ UNCHANGED <<bayLock, phase, target>>

Load == /\ phase = "fine"
        /\ target \in Bays
        /\ bay[target] > 0
        /\ bay' = [bay EXCEPT ![target] = @ - 1]
        /\ ship' = ship + 1
        /\ UNCHANGED <<bayLock, phase, target>>

Release == /\ phase \in {"coarse", "fine"}
           /\ target \in Bays
           /\ bayLock' = [bayLock EXCEPT ![target] = "free"]
           /\ phase' = "idle"
           /\ target' = "none"
           /\ UNCHANGED <<ship, bay>>

AdminOverride == /\ phase \in {"coarse", "fine"}
                 /\ target \in Bays
                 /\ bayLock' = [bayLock EXCEPT ![target] = "free"]
                 /\ phase' = "idle"
                 /\ target' = "none"
                 /\ UNCHANGED <<ship, bay>>

Next == AcquireCoarse \/ AcquireFine \/ Unload \/ Load \/ Release \/ AdminOverride

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ContainersConserved == ship + SumB(Bays) = TOTAL
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS Bays = {b1, b2} TOTAL = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT ContainersConserved
nl:
A container-ship crane yard unloads steel containers from a ship into a storage yard divided into bays, where each bay holds several stacking slots. A single gantry crane moves containers, and to do so safely it must take locks in a strict hierarchy: first the coarse lock on a whole bay, then the fine lock on the working area inside that bay. Only after holding both may the crane transfer a container, either lifting one off the ship into the current bay or returning one from the bay back onto the ship. When finished the crane releases its locks and becomes idle again. A privileged yard supervisor may issue an administrative override that forcibly clears whatever lock the crane holds and returns the crane to idle, for instance to recover from a stuck operation; this override only clears locks and never itself moves any container. Containers are physical and conserved: every container is always either on the ship or sitting in exactly one bay, and the override, the locking, and the transfers only ever relocate them.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of containers on the ship plus the number stored across all yard bays always equals the fixed total the yard began with.

---- MODULE W4Od7m5p3t5 ----
EXTENDS FiniteSets, Integers
CONSTANTS Slots, Jobs, Controllers, QUORUM, CMAX
ASSUME QUORUM \in Nat /\ CMAX \in Nat

VARIABLES ledger, proposal, ayes, jobsRun
vars == <<ledger, proposal, ayes, jobsRun>>

Pairs == {[slot |-> s, job |-> j] : s \in Slots, j \in Jobs}
SlotTaken(s) == \E p \in ledger : p.slot = s

Init == /\ ledger = {}
        /\ proposal = [s \in Slots |-> "none"]
        /\ ayes = [s \in Slots |-> {}]
        /\ jobsRun = [s \in Slots |-> 0]

Propose(s, j) == /\ proposal[s] = "none"
                 /\ ~SlotTaken(s)
                 /\ proposal' = [proposal EXCEPT ![s] = j]
                 /\ ayes' = [ayes EXCEPT ![s] = {}]
                 /\ UNCHANGED <<ledger, jobsRun>>

Vote(s, c) == /\ proposal[s] # "none"
              /\ c \notin ayes[s]
              /\ ayes' = [ayes EXCEPT ![s] = @ \cup {c}]
              /\ UNCHANGED <<ledger, proposal, jobsRun>>

Commit(s) == /\ proposal[s] # "none"
             /\ Cardinality(ayes[s]) >= QUORUM
             /\ ~SlotTaken(s)
             /\ ledger' = ledger \cup {[slot |-> s, job |-> proposal[s]]}
             /\ proposal' = [proposal EXCEPT ![s] = "none"]
             /\ ayes' = [ayes EXCEPT ![s] = {}]
             /\ UNCHANGED jobsRun

Release(s) == /\ SlotTaken(s)
              /\ ledger' = {p \in ledger : p.slot # s}
              /\ jobsRun' = [jobsRun EXCEPT ![s] = 0]
              /\ UNCHANGED <<proposal, ayes>>

AdminClear(s) == /\ proposal[s] # "none"
                 /\ proposal' = [proposal EXCEPT ![s] = "none"]
                 /\ ayes' = [ayes EXCEPT ![s] = {}]
                 /\ UNCHANGED <<ledger, jobsRun>>

Process(s) == /\ SlotTaken(s)
              /\ jobsRun[s] < CMAX
              /\ jobsRun' = [jobsRun EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
              /\ UNCHANGED <<ledger, proposal, ayes>>

Next == \/ \E s \in Slots, j \in Jobs : Propose(s, j)
        \/ \E s \in Slots, c \in Controllers : Vote(s, c)
        \/ \E s \in Slots : Commit(s) \/ Release(s) \/ AdminClear(s) \/ Process(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

SlotNotDoubleAllocated ==
    \A p, q \in ledger : p.slot = q.slot => p.job = q.job
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS Slots = {s1, s2} Jobs = {j1, j2} Controllers = {c1, c2, c3} QUORUM = 2 CMAX = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT SlotNotDoubleAllocated
nl:
A container-ship crane yard assigns physical parking slots on the quay to inbound container jobs, and each slot must belong to at most one job. Assignments are not made unilaterally: a controller proposes giving a particular free slot to a particular job, then a group of independent yard controllers votes on the proposal, and the assignment is only committed once a quorum of controllers has approved it and the slot is still free. Committing records the slot-to-job assignment in the yard's allocation ledger. While a slot is committed to a job, the crane may run processing passes on it, up to a bounded number. A job's slot can later be released, removing its ledger entry so the slot is available again. A privileged shift supervisor holds an administrative override that can forcibly clear a stuck or contested proposal, discarding its accumulated votes so the slot can be proposed afresh; the override never itself writes an assignment into the ledger. The danger the yard guards against is a race in which the same slot ends up committed to two different jobs at once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the allocation ledger never records the same slot assigned to two different jobs at the same time.

---- MODULE W4Od13m0p4t2 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANTS CAP, INITPOOL, K
ASSUME CAP \in Nat /\ INITPOOL \in Nat /\ K \in Nat /\ K >= 1

VARIABLES stockA, stockB, pool, version, pendA, pendB
vars == <<stockA, stockB, pool, version, pendA, pendB>>

IDLE == -1
Bump(v) == (v + 1) % K

Init == /\ stockA = 0 /\ stockB = 0
        /\ pool = INITPOOL
        /\ version = 0
        /\ pendA = IDLE /\ pendB = IDLE

BeginA == /\ pendA = IDLE
          /\ pendA' = version
          /\ UNCHANGED <<stockA, stockB, pool, version, pendB>>
BeginB == /\ pendB = IDLE
          /\ pendB' = version
          /\ UNCHANGED <<stockA, stockB, pool, version, pendA>>

CommitA == /\ pendA # IDLE
           /\ pendA = version
           /\ pool > 0
           /\ stockA < CAP
           /\ stockA' = stockA + 1
           /\ pool' = pool - 1
           /\ version' = Bump(version)
           /\ pendA' = IDLE
           /\ UNCHANGED <<stockB, pendB>>
CommitB == /\ pendB # IDLE
           /\ pendB = version
           /\ pool > 0
           /\ stockB < CAP
           /\ stockB' = stockB + 1
           /\ pool' = pool - 1
           /\ version' = Bump(version)
           /\ pendB' = IDLE
           /\ UNCHANGED <<stockA, pendA>>

RetryA == /\ pendA # IDLE
          /\ pendA # version
          /\ pendA' = version
          /\ UNCHANGED <<stockA, stockB, pool, version, pendB>>
RetryB == /\ pendB # IDLE
          /\ pendB # version
          /\ pendB' = version
          /\ UNCHANGED <<stockA, stockB, pool, version, pendA>>

AbandonA == /\ pendA # IDLE
            /\ pendA' = IDLE
            /\ UNCHANGED <<stockA, stockB, pool, version, pendB>>
AbandonB == /\ pendB # IDLE
            /\ pendB' = IDLE
            /\ UNCHANGED <<stockA, stockB, pool, version, pendA>>

Next == BeginA \/ BeginB \/ CommitA \/ CommitB \/ RetryA \/ RetryB
        \/ AbandonA \/ AbandonB

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

RackWithinCapacity == stockA <= CAP /\ stockB <= CAP
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS CAP = 2 INITPOOL = 3 K = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT RackWithinCapacity
nl:
A beverage company runs a network of vending machines that all restock from one shared regional warehouse pool. Two machines operate independently but pull cans from the same finite pool, and each machine has a display rack with a strict capacity that must never be overfilled. To avoid corrupting the shared pool count, each machine restocks using optimistic concurrency: it first reads the pool's current version stamp, then attempts to commit a single-can transfer only if the version stamp is still unchanged and the pool is non-empty and its own rack has room. A successful commit moves one can from the pool to the rack and advances the pool's version stamp. If a machine finds that the version stamp has moved since it read it, meaning the other machine committed in between, it either abandons the attempt outright and returns to idle, or retries by re-reading the current stamp. The company must guarantee that this optimistic scheme, even under interleaved retries, never lets either machine's rack exceed its capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: neither vending machine's rack ever holds more cans than its fixed rack capacity.

---- MODULE W4Od2m5p5t0 ----
EXTENDS FiniteSets, Integers
CONSTANTS Robots, Orders, QUORUM
ASSUME QUORUM \in Nat

VARIABLES status, proposal, votes, shipped, manifest
vars == <<status, proposal, votes, shipped, manifest>>

UpRobots == {r \in Robots : status[r] = "up"}

TypeOK == /\ status \in [Robots -> {"up", "crashed"}]
          /\ proposal \in Orders \cup {"none"}
          /\ votes \subseteq Robots
          /\ shipped \in 0..3
          /\ manifest \in Orders \cup {"none"}

Init == /\ status = [r \in Robots |-> "up"]
        /\ proposal = "none"
        /\ votes = {}
        /\ shipped = 0
        /\ manifest = "none"

Crash == /\ \A r \in Robots : status[r] = "up"
         /\ \E r \in Robots :
              status' = [status EXCEPT ![r] = "crashed"]
         /\ UNCHANGED <<proposal, votes, shipped, manifest>>

Propose(o) == /\ proposal = "none"
              /\ proposal' = o
              /\ votes' = {}
              /\ UNCHANGED <<status, shipped, manifest>>

Vote(r) == /\ status[r] = "up"
           /\ proposal # "none"
           /\ r \notin votes
           /\ votes' = votes \cup {r}
           /\ UNCHANGED <<status, proposal, shipped, manifest>>

Retract == /\ proposal # "none"
           /\ proposal' = "none"
           /\ votes' = {}
           /\ UNCHANGED <<status, shipped, manifest>>

Ship == /\ proposal # "none"
        /\ shipped = 0
        /\ Cardinality(votes \cap UpRobots) >= QUORUM
        /\ shipped' = shipped + 1
        /\ manifest' = proposal
        /\ proposal' = "none"
        /\ votes' = {}
        /\ UNCHANGED status

Next == Crash \/ Ship \/ Retract
        \/ (\E o \in Orders : Propose(o))
        \/ (\E r \in Robots : Vote(r))

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ShipOnlyOnce ==
    /\ shipped <= 1
    /\ (shipped = 1 => manifest # "none")
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS Robots = {r1, r2, r3} Orders = {o1, o2} QUORUM = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT ShipOnlyOnce
nl:
A fleet of warehouse robots must jointly perform one irreversible action: sealing and shipping a single high-value order out of the building, after which it cannot be recalled. The decision is made by quorum voting. Any robot may propose that a particular order be the one shipped, other robots then cast approving votes for that proposal, and the seal-and-ship only fires once a quorum of still-operational robots has approved and no shipment has yet gone out. Firing records the shipped order on the frozen manifest and is counted as the one irreversible dispatch. A proposal that has not yet shipped may be retracted so a different order can be proposed instead. Robots are unreliable: a single robot may crash silently at any time, after which it stops casting votes, though the remaining robots can still reach quorum. The overriding requirement is that no matter how proposals, votes, retractions, and a crash interleave, the fleet ships at most one order, exactly once, and never twice.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the irreversible seal-and-ship dispatch is performed at most one time over the entire run, and if it has happened the shipped order is recorded on the manifest.

---- MODULE W4Od16m9p1t0 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANTS Stations, Updates, MAXEPOCH
ASSUME MAXEPOCH \in Nat

VARIABLES applied, acked, epoch, status, pending
vars == <<applied, acked, epoch, status, pending>>

Init == /\ applied = {}
        /\ acked = [w \in Stations |-> {}]
        /\ epoch = 0
        /\ status = [w \in Stations |-> "up"]
        /\ pending = [w \in Stations |-> "none"]

Submit(w, u) == /\ status[w] = "up"
                /\ pending[w] = "none"
                /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![w] = u]
                /\ UNCHANGED <<applied, acked, epoch, status>>

Commit(w) == /\ status[w] = "up"
             /\ pending[w] # "none"
             /\ applied' = applied \cup {pending[w]}
             /\ acked' = [acked EXCEPT ![w] = @ \cup {pending[w]}]
             /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![w] = "none"]
             /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, status>>

Reconfigure == /\ epoch < MAXEPOCH
               /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
               /\ applied' = applied
               /\ UNCHANGED <<acked, status, pending>>

Crash == /\ \A w \in Stations : status[w] = "up"
         /\ \E w \in Stations :
              status' = [status EXCEPT ![w] = "crashed"]
         /\ UNCHANGED <<applied, acked, epoch, pending>>

Next == \/ \E w \in Stations, u \in Updates : Submit(w, u)
        \/ \E w \in Stations : Commit(w)
        \/ Reconfigure
        \/ Crash

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoAcknowledgedUpdateLost ==
    \A w \in Stations : acked[w] \subseteq applied
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS Stations = {w1, w2} Updates = {u1, u2} MAXEPOCH = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoAcknowledgedUpdateLost
nl:
A hospital pharmacy runs prescription-dispensing stations that all update one shared electronic medication record for a patient. Each station submits updates such as adding a dispensed drug, and once a station is told its update succeeded it must never see that update silently vanish from the shared record. The system runs in numbered configuration epochs; periodically a reconfiguration advances the epoch, for example when dispensing responsibility is handed to a new controller, and a correct reconfiguration must carry every already-incorporated update forward intact rather than rebuilding the record from scratch and dropping some. A station first stages one pending update, then commits it, which incorporates the update into the shared record and marks it acknowledged for that station. Stations are not fully reliable: a single station may crash silently and stop submitting, but the remaining station keeps operating. The overriding correctness requirement is that any update a station has been told succeeded remains present in the shared record thereafter, across commits by other stations and across epoch reconfigurations.
SAFETY PROPERTY: every update that any station has had acknowledged as successful is still present in the shared medication record.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od12m3p4t2 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANTS Sites, CAP, INITPOOL, MAXTERM
ASSUME CAP \in Nat /\ INITPOOL \in Nat /\ MAXTERM \in Nat

VARIABLES leader, alive, store, pool, term
vars == <<leader, alive, store, pool, term>>

Init == /\ leader = "none"
        /\ alive = [s \in Sites |-> TRUE]
        /\ store = [s \in Sites |-> 0]
        /\ pool = INITPOOL
        /\ term = 0

Elect(s) == /\ alive[s]
            /\ leader = "none"
            /\ leader' = s
            /\ term' = IF term < MAXTERM THEN term + 1 ELSE term
            /\ UNCHANGED <<alive, store, pool>>

Failover(s) == /\ leader = s
               /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![s] = FALSE]
               /\ leader' = "none"
               /\ UNCHANGED <<store, pool, term>>

Revive(s) == /\ ~alive[s]
             /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![s] = TRUE]
             /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, store, pool, term>>

StockIn == /\ leader # "none"
           /\ pool > 0
           /\ store[leader] < CAP
           /\ store' = [store EXCEPT ![leader] = @ + 1]
           /\ pool' = pool - 1
           /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive, term>>

Issue(s) == /\ store[s] > 0

        /\ claim = [r \in Routers |-> -1]

           /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![r] = -1]

Drones can crash silently, but only while idle, never mid-transmission; a single drone may drop out this way. If the drone that happens to hold the token has crashed, and no drone is transmitting, a swarm watchdog regenerates the token by reassigning it to some still-flying drone. EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANTS CAP, MAXGEN
ASSUME CAP \in Nat /\ MAXGEN \in Nat

Trackers == {"b1", "b2", "b3"}
NextR(t) == CASE t = "b1" -> "b2"
              [] t = "b2" -> "b3"
              [] OTHER    -> "b1"

vars == <<tokenHolder, tokenGen, phase, usedGen, stock>>

Init == /\ tokenHolder = "b1"
        /\ tokenGen = 0
        /\ phase = [t \in Trackers |-> "idle"]
        /\ usedGen = [t \in Trackers |-> -1]
        /\ stock = 0

Pass(t) == /\ tokenHolder = t
           /\ phase[t] = "idle"
           /\ tokenHolder' = NextR(t)
           /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenGen, phase, usedGen, stock>>

Arm(t) == /\ tokenHolder = t
          /\ phase[t] = "idle"
          /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "armed"]
          /\ usedGen' = [usedGen EXCEPT ![t] = tokenGen]
          /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenHolder, tokenGen, stock>>

Write(t) == /\ tokenHolder = t
            /\ phase[t] = "armed"
            /\ usedGen[t] = tokenGen
            /\ stock < CAP
            /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "writing"]
            /\ stock' = stock + 1
            /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenHolder, tokenGen, usedGen>>

Finish(t) == /\ phase[t] = "writing"
             /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "idle"]
             /\ usedGen' = [usedGen EXCEPT ![t] = -1]
             /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenHolder, tokenGen, stock>>

DropStale(t) == /\ phase[t] \in {"armed", "writing"}
                /\ (tokenHolder # t \/ usedGen[t] # tokenGen)
                /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "idle"]
                /\ usedGen' = [usedGen EXCEPT ![t] = -1]
                /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenHolder, tokenGen, stock>>

AdminRevoke == /\ tokenGen' = IF tokenGen < MAXGEN THEN tokenGen + 1 ELSE tokenGen
               /\ phase' = [t \in Trackers |-> "idle"]
               /\ usedGen' = [t \in Trackers |-> -1]
               /\ \E e \in Trackers : tokenHolder' = e
               /\ UNCHANGED stock

Next == \/ \E t \in Trackers : Pass(t) \/ Arm(t) \/ Write(t) \/ Finish(t) \/ DropStale(t)
        \/ AdminRevoke

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoUnauthorizedWriter ==
    \A t \in Trackers :
        phase[t] \in {"armed", "writing"} =>
            (tokenHolder = t /\ usedGen[t] = tokenGen)

CONSTANTS CAP = 2 MAXGEN = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoUnauthorizedWriter
nl:
A blood-bank inventory service runs several tracker nodes arranged in a token ring, and only the node holding the ring token may write adjustments to the shared inventory count. To write, a node first arms itself by recording the token's current generation number, then performs the write only while it still holds the token and its recorded generation still matches the live generation. The token is passed to the next node in the ring only while the passing node is idle, so a node never yields the token mid-write. A privileged supervisor holds an administrative override: at any time it can revoke and reissue the token, which advances the token generation, reassigns the token to some node, and forces every node back to idle, cancelling any armed or in-progress write. Because the override can bump the generation and move the token, an armed or writing node whose generation is stale or which no longer holds the token is unauthorized and must not proceed. The service must guarantee that any node that is armed or writing genuinely holds the token and carries the current generation.

---- MODULE W4Od2m3p5t1 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANTS Robots, MAXTERM
ASSUME MAXTERM \in Nat

VARIABLES term, leader, alive, msgs, dispatched, dispatchTerm
vars == <<term, leader, alive, msgs, dispatched, dispatchTerm>>

Init == /\ term = 0
        /\ leader = "none"
        /\ alive = [r \in Robots |-> TRUE]
        /\ msgs = {}
        /\ dispatched = 0
        /\ dispatchTerm = -1

Elect(r) == /\ alive[r]
            /\ leader = "none"
            /\ leader' = r
            /\ term' = IF term < MAXTERM THEN term + 1 ELSE term
            /\ UNCHANGED <<alive, msgs, dispatched, dispatchTerm>>

Failover(r) == /\ leader = r
               /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![r] = FALSE]
               /\ leader' = "none"
               /\ UNCHANGED <<term, msgs, dispatched, dispatchTerm>>

Revive(r) == /\ ~alive[r]
             /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![r] = TRUE]
             /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, msgs, dispatched, dispatchTerm>>

IssueCommand(r) == /\ leader = r
                   /\ alive[r]
                   /\ msgs' = msgs \cup {[type |-> "dispatch", term |-> term]}
                   /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, alive, dispatched, dispatchTerm>>

Deliver == /\ \E m \in msgs :
                /\ m.type = "dispatch"
                /\ m.term = term
                /\ dispatched = 0
                /\ dispatched' = dispatched + 1
                /\ dispatchTerm' = term
                /\ msgs' = msgs \ {m}
           /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, alive>>

DropStale == /\ \E m \in msgs :
                  /\ m.term # term
                  /\ msgs' = msgs \ {m}
             /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, alive, dispatched, dispatchTerm>>

Next == \/ \E r \in Robots : Elect(r) \/ Failover(r) \/ Revive(r) \/ IssueCommand(r)
        \/ Deliver \/ DropStale

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TruckDispatchedAtMostOnce == dispatched <= 1

CONSTANTS Robots = {r1, r2} MAXTERM = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next

nl:
A warehouse robot fleet must dispatch one outbound truck exactly once: sealing and sending the truck is irreversible and must never happen twice. The robots coordinate through an elected leader. When there is no leader, an available robot can be elected, which advances the election term. The current leader may fail over, going offline and vacating the leadership so another robot can be elected in a later term; a failed robot can be revived. Only the leader issues dispatch commands, and each command is stamped with the term in which it was issued. The warehouse messaging fabric does not preserve order, so dispatch commands sit in an unordered pool and may be delivered late or out of order, including a stale command left over from a deposed leader. The truck actually departs when a dispatch command whose term matches the current term is delivered and the truck has not already been sent. Stale commands whose term no longer matches may be discarded. Despite failovers and reordered, stale commands, the fleet must guarantee the truck is dispatched at most once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the irreversible truck dispatch occurs at most one time over the whole run, no matter how elections, failovers, and reordered stale commands interleave.

---- MODULE W4Od0m8p1t4 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANTS Schedulers
Slots == {"sl1", "sl2"}

VARIABLES roomLock, slotLock, target, schedule, acked, capacity
vars == <<roomLock, slotLock, target, schedule, acked, capacity>>

OpenSlot(sl) == \/ sl = "sl1"
                \/ (sl = "sl2" /\ capacity >= 2)

Init == /\ roomLock = "free"
        /\ slotLock = [sl \in Slots |-> "free"]
        /\ target = [s \in Schedulers |-> "none"]
        /\ schedule = {}
        /\ acked = [s \in Schedulers |-> {}]
        /\ capacity = 1

AcquireCoarse(s, sl) == /\ roomLock = "free"
                        /\ target[s] = "none"
                        /\ roomLock' = s
                        /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![s] = sl]
                        /\ UNCHANGED <<slotLock, schedule, acked, capacity>>

AcquireFine(s) == /\ roomLock = s
                  /\ target[s] \in Slots
                  /\ slotLock[target[s]] = "free"
                  /\ slotLock' = [slotLock EXCEPT ![target[s]] = s]
                  /\ UNCHANGED <<roomLock, target, schedule, acked, capacity>>

Book(s) == /\ roomLock = s
           /\ target[s] \in Slots
           /\ slotLock[target[s]] = s
           /\ OpenSlot(target[s])
           /\ target[s] \notin schedule
           /\ schedule' = schedule \cup {target[s]}
           /\ acked' = [acked EXCEPT ![s] = @ \cup {target[s]}]
           /\ UNCHANGED <<roomLock, slotLock, target, capacity>>

Release(s) == /\ roomLock = s
              /\ target[s] \in Slots
              /\ roomLock' = "free"
              /\ slotLock' = [slotLock EXCEPT ![target[s]] = "free"]
              /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![s] = "none"]
              /\ UNCHANGED <<schedule, acked, capacity>>

CapacityChange == /\ capacity' = IF capacity = 1 THEN 2 ELSE 1
                  /\ UNCHANGED <<roomLock, slotLock, target, schedule, acked>>

Next == \/ \E s \in Schedulers, sl \in Slots : AcquireCoarse(s, sl)
        \/ \E s \in Schedulers : AcquireFine(s) \/ Book(s) \/ Release(s)
        \/ CapacityChange

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoAcknowledgedBookingLost ==
    \A s \in Schedulers : acked[s] \subseteq schedule
====

CONSTANTS Schedulers = {x, y}
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoAcknowledgedBookingLost
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler lets surgeons book time slots in a shared operating room, recording confirmed bookings in one shared schedule. To write a booking a surgeon must take locks in a strict hierarchy: first the coarse lock on the whole operating room, then the fine lock on the specific time slot, and only while holding both may the surgeon confirm the booking, which adds the slot to the shared schedule and marks it acknowledged for that surgeon. When done the surgeon releases the slot lock and the room lock together. The room's capacity changes at runtime: an administrator can open or close the later time slot, switching between a one-slot and a two-slot configuration, so a slot may only be freshly booked while it is currently open. Crucially, closing a slot must never erase an already-confirmed booking; a surgery that was booked stays booked even if capacity is later reduced. The scheduler must guarantee no acknowledged booking is ever lost: every booking a surgeon has had confirmed remains present in the shared schedule.
SAFETY PROPERTY: every booking that any surgeon has had acknowledged as confirmed is still present in the shared operating-room schedule.

---- MODULE W4Od10m5p4t0 ----
EXTENDS FiniteSets, Integers
CONSTANTS Blocks, Controllers, QUORUM, CAP
ASSUME QUORUM \in Nat /\ CAP \in Nat

VARIABLES occ, proposal, ayes, cstatus
vars == <<occ, proposal, ayes, cstatus>>

UpControllers == {c \in Controllers : cstatus[c] = "up"}

Init == /\ occ = [b \in Blocks |-> 0]
        /\ proposal = [b \in Blocks |-> "none"]
        /\ ayes = [b \in Blocks |-> {}]
        /\ cstatus = [c \in Controllers |-> "up"]

Propose(b) == /\ occ[b] < CAP
              /\ proposal[b] = "none"
              /\ proposal' = [proposal EXCEPT ![b] = "admit"]
              /\ ayes' = [ayes EXCEPT ![b] = {}]
              /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, cstatus>>

Vote(b, c) == /\ cstatus[c] = "up"
              /\ proposal[b] = "admit"
              /\ c \notin ayes[b]
              /\ ayes' = [ayes EXCEPT ![b] = @ \cup {c}]
              /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, proposal, cstatus>>

Admit(b) == /\ proposal[b] = "admit"
            /\ Cardinality(ayes[b] \cap UpControllers) >= QUORUM
            /\ occ[b] < CAP
            /\ occ' = [occ EXCEPT ![b] = @ + 1]
            /\ proposal' = [proposal EXCEPT ![b] = "none"]
            /\ ayes' = [ayes EXCEPT ![b] = {}]
            /\ UNCHANGED cstatus

Reset(b) == /\ proposal[b] = "admit"
            /\ proposal' = [proposal EXCEPT ![b] = "none"]
            /\ ayes' = [ayes EXCEPT ![b] = {}]
            /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, cstatus>>

Depart(b) == /\ occ[b] > 0
             /\ occ' = [occ EXCEPT ![b] = @ - 1]
             /\ UNCHANGED <<proposal, ayes, cstatus>>

Crash == /\ \A c \in Controllers : cstatus[c] = "up"
         /\ \E c \in Controllers : cstatus' = [cstatus EXCEPT ![c] = "crashed"]
         /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, proposal, ayes>>

Next == \/ \E b \in Blocks : Propose(b) \/ Admit(b) \/ Reset(b) \/ Depart(b)
        \/ \E b \in Blocks, c \in Controllers : Vote(b, c)
        \/ Crash

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

BlockWithinCapacity == \A b \in Blocks : occ[b] <= CAP
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS Blocks = {k1, k2} Controllers = {c1, c2, c3} QUORUM = 2 CAP = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT BlockWithinCapacity
nl:
A subway signalling system controls admission of trains into track blocks, where each block can safely hold only a bounded number of trains at once. Admitting a train into a block is not decided by a single signal box: a quorum of independent signal controllers must approve it. A controller proposes admitting a train into a block that still has room, other controllers cast approving votes, and the train is admitted only once a quorum of still-operational controllers has approved and the block is genuinely below its capacity. A pending admission proposal may be reset. Trains already in a block may depart, freeing space. Controllers are not perfectly reliable: a single controller may crash silently and stop voting, but the remaining controllers can still form a quorum. The overriding safety requirement is that no matter how proposals, votes, admissions, departures, and a controller crash interleave, no block ever holds more trains than its capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no track block ever holds more trains than its fixed safe capacity.

---- MODULE W4Od10m9p6t3 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANTS Sectors, Controllers, MAXEPOCH, TMAX
ASSUME MAXEPOCH \in Nat /\ TMAX \in Nat

VARIABLES epoch, owner, view, arming, armEpoch, throughput
vars == <<epoch, owner, view, arming, armEpoch, throughput>>

Init == /\ epoch = 0
        /\ owner = [s \in Sectors |-> CHOOSE c \in Controllers : TRUE]
        /\ view = [c \in Controllers |-> 0]
        /\ arming = [s \in Sectors |-> "none"]
        /\ armEpoch = [s \in Sectors |-> -1]
        /\ throughput = 0

Refresh(c) == /\ view[c] < epoch
              /\ view' = [view EXCEPT ![c] = epoch]
              /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, owner, arming, armEpoch, throughput>>

Reconfigure == /\ epoch < MAXEPOCH
               /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
               /\ \E newOwner \in [Sectors -> Controllers] : owner' = newOwner
               /\ arming' = [s \in Sectors |-> "none"]
               /\ armEpoch' = [s \in Sectors |-> -1]
               /\ UNCHANGED <<view, throughput>>

Arm(c, s) == /\ owner[s] = c
             /\ view[c] = epoch
             /\ arming[s] = "none"
             /\ arming' = [arming EXCEPT ![s] = c]
             /\ armEpoch' = [armEpoch EXCEPT ![s] = epoch]
             /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, owner, view, throughput>>

Execute(s) == /\ arming[s] # "none"
              /\ owner[s] = arming[s]
              /\ armEpoch[s] = epoch
              /\ throughput < TMAX
              /\ throughput' = throughput + 1
              /\ arming' = [arming EXCEPT ![s] = "none"]
              /\ armEpoch' = [armEpoch EXCEPT ![s] = -1]
              /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, owner, view>>

Abort(s) == /\ arming[s] # "none"
            /\ arming' = [arming EXCEPT ![s] = "none"]
            /\ armEpoch' = [armEpoch EXCEPT ![s] = -1]
            /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, owner, view, throughput>>

Next == \/ \E c \in Controllers : Refresh(c)
        \/ \E c \in Controllers, s \in Sectors : Arm(c, s)
        \/ \E s \in Sectors : Execute(s) \/ Abort(s)
        \/ Reconfigure

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoStaleArming ==
    \A s \in Sectors :
        arming[s] # "none" => (owner[s] = arming[s] /\ armEpoch[s] = epoch)

CONSTANTS Sectors = {sec1, sec2} Controllers = {c1, c2} MAXEPOCH = 2 TMAX = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoStaleArming
nl:
A subway signalling system divides the line into control sectors, and in each numbered configuration epoch every sector is assigned to exactly one authorized controller. Controllers each keep a cached view of which epoch they believe is current, and because a controller may be slow it can lag behind the true epoch, though it never fails outright and eventually catches up by refreshing its view. To issue a sector command a controller first arms it, which is only allowed if that controller is the sector's current owner and its cached view matches the live epoch, and the arming records the epoch used. It then executes the command only while it is still the owner and the armed epoch still matches the live epoch. The line is periodically reconfigured: a reconfiguration advances the epoch, reassigns sector ownership, and cancels every outstanding arming, so a slow controller acting on an old assignment is stale and unauthorized. Armings may also be aborted. The system must guarantee that any armed command genuinely belongs to the sector's current owner and carries the live epoch, so no stale or unauthorized controller ever acts.
SAFETY PROPERTY: every outstanding sector arming belongs to that sector's current owner and records the live epoch, so no stale or unauthorized controller commands a sector.

---- MODULE W4Od11m8p2t2 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANTS Printers, TOTAL
ASSUME TOTAL \in Nat

VARIABLES spool, inPrinter, coarseLock, fineLock, worker, active
vars == <<spool, inPrinter, coarseLock, fineLock, worker, active>>

RECURSIVE SumP(_)
SumP(S) == IF S = {} THEN 0
           ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN inPrinter[x] + SumP(S \ {x})

Init == /\ spool = TOTAL
        /\ inPrinter = [p \in Printers |-> 0]
        /\ coarseLock = [p \in Printers |-> "free"]
        /\ fineLock = [p \in Printers |-> "free"]
        /\ worker = "idle"
        /\ active = "none"

AcquireCoarse(p) == /\ worker = "idle"
                    /\ coarseLock[p] = "free"
                    /\ coarseLock' = [coarseLock EXCEPT ![p] = "held"]
                    /\ worker' = "coarse"
                    /\ active' = p
                    /\ UNCHANGED <<spool, inPrinter, fineLock>>

AcquireFine == /\ worker = "coarse"
               /\ active \in Printers
               /\ fineLock[active] = "free"
               /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT ![active] = "held"]
               /\ worker' = "fine"
               /\ UNCHANGED <<spool, inPrinter, coarseLock, active>>

Load == /\ worker = "fine"
        /\ active \in Printers
        /\ spool > 0
        /\ spool' = spool - 1
        /\ inPrinter' = [inPrinter EXCEPT ![active] = @ + 1]
        /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, fineLock, worker, active>>

Unload == /\ worker = "fine"
          /\ active \in Printers
          /\ inPrinter[active] > 0
          /\ inPrinter' = [inPrinter EXCEPT ![active] = @ - 1]
          /\ spool' = spool + 1
          /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, fineLock, worker, active>>

Release == /\ worker \in {"coarse", "fine"}
           /\ active \in Printers
           /\ coarseLock' = [coarseLock EXCEPT ![active] = "free"]
           /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT ![active] = "free"]
           /\ worker' = "idle"
           /\ active' = "none"
           /\ UNCHANGED <<spool, inPrinter>>

Next == \/ \E p \in Printers : AcquireCoarse(p)
        \/ AcquireFine \/ Load \/ Unload \/ Release

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

====

CONSTANTS Printers = {pa, pb} TOTAL = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT JobsConserved
nl:
A print shop runs a job spooler that feeds two independent printers from one shared spool pool of pending print jobs. Jobs are conserved: every job is always either waiting in the shared spool or loaded in exactly one of the two printers, and the spooler only ever moves jobs between these places, never creating or destroying them. A single spooler worker moves jobs, and to touch a printer safely it takes locks in a strict hierarchy: first the coarse lock on the whole printer, then the fine lock on that printer's feed tray. Only while holding both may it load one job from the shared spool into the printer, or unload one job from the printer back into the spool. When finished it releases both locks and becomes idle. Because the two printers draw from and return to the same shared spool, the shop must be certain that all this locking and moving merely shuffles jobs between the spool and the two printers and never changes the grand total of jobs in the system.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of jobs waiting in the shared spool plus the jobs loaded in the first printer plus the jobs loaded in the second printer always equals the fixed total number of jobs.

---- MODULE W4Od9m7p3t0 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANTS Agents, Slots

VARIABLES ledger, status, shed, fenced
vars == <<ledger, status, shed, fenced>>

Pairs == {[slot |-> sl, agent |-> a] : sl \in Slots, a \in Agents}
SlotFree(sl) == ~ \E p \in ledger : p.slot = sl

Init == /\ ledger = {}
        /\ status = [a \in Agents |-> "up"]
        /\ shed = {}
        /\ fenced = {}

Claim(a, sl) == /\ status[a] = "up"
                /\ SlotFree(sl)
                /\ ledger' = ledger \cup {[slot |-> sl, agent |-> a]}
                /\ UNCHANGED <<status, shed, fenced>>

Release(a, sl) == /\ status[a] = "up"
                  /\ [slot |-> sl, agent |-> a] \in ledger
                  /\ ledger' = ledger \ {[slot |-> sl, agent |-> a]}
                  /\ shed' = shed \ {[slot |-> sl, agent |-> a]}
                  /\ UNCHANGED <<status, fenced>>

Shed(a, sl) == /\ status[a] = "up"
               /\ [slot |-> sl, agent |-> a] \in ledger
               /\ [slot |-> sl, agent |-> a] \notin shed
               /\ shed' = shed \cup {[slot |-> sl, agent |-> a]}
               /\ UNCHANGED <<ledger, status, fenced>>

         /\ \E a \in Agents : status' = [status EXCEPT ![a] = "crashed"]
         /\ UNCHANGED <<ledger, shed, fenced>>

                    /\ p.slot = sl
                    /\ status[p.agent] = "crashed"
                    /\ ledger' = ledger \ {p}
                    /\ shed' = shed \ {p}
                    /\ fenced' = fenced \cup {p.agent}
               /\ UNCHANGED status

        \/ \E sl \in Slots : Reclaim(sl)
        \/ Crash

nl:
A power-grid load shedder lets control agents claim exclusive load-shedding slots, one per sheddable feeder circuit, using a compare-and-swap register for each slot. To claim a slot an agent performs an atomic compare-and-swap: it checks that the slot's register reads free and, in the same indivisible step, stamps the register with its own identity and records the slot in its private set of held slots. Only the agent that stamped a slot may release it, which atomically resets the register to free and drops the slot from its held set. While holding a slot an agent may shed load on that feeder. Agents can crash silently: a single agent may drop offline without releasing its slots, and its stamped registers stay stamped. To recover capacity a grid watchdog may fence a crashed agent, reclaiming a slot the crashed agent still holds by resetting the register to free, clearing it from that agent's held set, and recording that agent on the fenced-agent roster. The controlling requirement is that no single shedding slot is ever simultaneously held by two different agents.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no load-shedding slot is ever held by two different control agents at the same time.
